pass_a_gloss: Tome 3. [Lemma, Isaiah 30:27-28:] Behold, the name of the Lord comes through much time, the wrath burning with glory; the oracle of his lips, an oracle full of anger; and the anger of his wrath will eat like fire. And his breath, like water dragging in a ravine, will come as far as the neck and will be divided, to trouble nations upon vain error, and vain error will pursue them, and will take them according to their face. Having said very well that the light of the sun will be sevenfold for those who believe in Christ, at that time at which he heals the bruise of his people, he usefully adds that the divine wrath will be also against Satan, who bruised, and against the demons with him. For their tyranny against us was not going to come unceasing, and the strength unshaken, especially the Saviour of all, Christ, having shone upon the race of men. And the word of the prophecy has come not as bare and unclothed, but rather overshadowed and deep. For it has been shaped as about the Assyrians, who sacked Jerusalem, and took all Judaea, and having beloved Israel captured by spear, returned home to their own [land], all but dancing over the divine glory, and having thought that they overpowered his worshippers even God not being willing. And indeed Rabshakeh called out to those on the wall, saying: Let not Hezekiah deceive you, saying that God will rescue Israel from my hand. Did the gods of the nations, rescuing, each rescue his own country from my hand? Having boasted over, then, and having babbled many things against the ineffable glory, those about whom the word is would be caught. And Israel having completed in captivity and in the slavery among them the seventieth year, the God of all rescued again and saved. For he brought them back into Judaea, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel leading at that time, who was of the tribe of Judah, and indeed also Joshua the great priest. So the force of the prophecy seems somehow, as far as concerns the visible of the things that happened, to make mention of the Chaldeans and of Babylon. But the true thoughts of the things said have come against the spiritual Assyrian, that is, Satan, to whom it has been said by God: In what manner a garment soaked in blood will not be clean, thus neither will you be clean, because [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Tomos 3. “Behold, the name of the Lord comes after a long time, wrath burning with glory; the oracle of His lips is an oracle full of wrath, and the wrath of His anger will devour like fire. And His breath, like water rushing in a ravine, will reach as far as the neck and be divided, to trouble the nations for vain error; and vain error will pursue them and seize them before their face” (Isaiah 30:27-28).

Having said very well that the light of the sun will be sevenfold for those who believe in Christ, at that time when He heals the bruise of His people (Isaiah 30:26), he usefully adds that the divine wrath will also be against Satan, who did the bruising, and against the demons with him. For their tyranny over us was not going to last without end, nor their strength to remain unshaken, above all once Christ, the Savior of all, had shone upon the human race.

The word of the prophecy is not bare and unclothed, as it were, but rather shadowed and deep. For it is framed as though about the Assyrians, who sacked Jerusalem and took all Judea, and, holding beloved Israel captive by the spear, went back to their own land, all but dancing in mockery over the divine glory and supposing that they had overpowered His worshippers even though God did not will it. Indeed Rabshakeh called out to those on the wall, saying: “Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, saying that God will deliver Israel out of my hand. Have the gods of the nations each delivered his own land out of my hand?” (Isaiah 36:14-18).

So those of whom the word speaks, having boasted greatly and babbled much against the ineffable glory, would be brought to judgment. And when Israel had spent seventy years in captivity and in slavery among them, the God of all rescued and saved him again. For He brought them back to Judea, under the leadership at that time of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, who was of the tribe of Judah, and of Joshua the high priest as well.

So the force of the prophecy seems, as far as what lies on the surface, to recall what befell the Chaldeans and Babylon. But the true meanings of what is said are directed against the spiritual Assyrian, that is, Satan, to whom God has said: “As a garment soaked in blood will not be clean, so neither will you be clean, because…” (Isaiah 14:19-20).
